Compare models on identical validation users and fixed per-user candidate sets; preserve the pinned evaluator and seed. Record paired hit indicators and estimate uncertainty in their difference using a paired user bootstrap or randomization test. For the four-category macro-average, resample users within each category, then average category differences equally. With 200 users/category, one changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points within a category, or 0.125 points in the macro-average. Report effect sizes, confidence intervals and discordant-user counts; small gains alone do not establish improvement. These recommendations apply paired-inference principles discussed in [Ihemelandu and Ekstrand](https://piret.info/pubs/2023/SIGIR23-InferenceAtScale). Such intervals are conditional on fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude candidate-sampling and training-seed variability.

Repeatedly selecting the best checkpoint or configuration on the same validation users creates selection optimism, even without training on validation labels. [Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html) show that overfitting model-selection criteria can rival differences between algorithms; [adaptive-holdout research](https://research.google/blog/the-reusable-holdout-preserving-validity-in-adaptive-data-analysis/) explains why repeated adaptive reuse undermines ordinary guarantees. Practical implications here: predefine checkpoint frequency, selection and stopping rules; log all comparisons; treat post-selection validation intervals as descriptive, not selection-adjusted evidence. Keep hidden test evaluation untouched until final selection. Rebootstrapping the selected winner does not remove selection bias.

Sampled HR@10 measures success against 99 sampled negatives, not the full catalog. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model orderings even in expectation. Fixed candidates improve comparability but cannot remove this bias. Retain the required metric and describe gains as benchmark-specific; avoid claims about full-catalog top-10 quality or real-user utility.
